title: Those cheese crystals are not salt

sources.title: Parmigiano Reggiano Consortium FAQ
claims: The visible white crystals described in the FAQ are tyrosine, an amino acid.
Tyrosine is released as proteins break down during maturation.
The crystals become larger and more numerous with longer maturation.

scenes.text: Those white crystals in Parmigiano Reggiano are not salt.
The cheese consortium identifies them as tyrosine, an amino acid.
As the cheese matures, enzymes break down milk proteins and release amino acids.
Tyrosine can gather into the little crystals you see inside the cheese.
Longer maturation brings more of them, and larger ones. Even the minimum ageing takes twelve months.
Now look at your next wedge. Do the crystals make it more tempting, or less?
